the use of a condom in combination with a microbicide gel, or microbicide gel only is a safe and effective way to protect against HIV infection and STI transmission.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated that home sampling is a feasible and acceptable method for STI screening in women.

the most important factors for a successful home-based screening program are a good understanding of the local context and a good collaboration between the local partners and the implementing organization.
the most effective and acceptable method of sampling for STI testing in young women is self-collected vaginal swabs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a clear need for more studies that examine the effectiveness of home-based testing for chlamydia and gonorrhoea in young women.

there is a need for more rigorous research to evaluate the comparative effectiveness of different sampling methods for sexually transmitted infection screening, especially in females aged 15-24 years.
there is a clear need to improve the sexual health of young women, particularly those with a history of child sexual abuse.
